issues.legal_issue: A surety-bond stamping defect does not require rejection of an application to set aside an ex parte decree where the bond was furnished within time, the defect was cured as directed by the court, and conflicting legal views had created uncertainty about the proper stamp.
material_facts: A small-causes suit was decreed ex parte when the defendant and his advocate were absent.
The defendant promptly applied for permission to provide security instead of depositing the full decretal amount in cash, and the court directed him to furnish a bond for the balance.
The defendant furnished the bond within the applicable period, but it bore a court-fee stamp rather than the stamp later held necessary by the High Court.
After the court pointed out the defect, the defendant supplied the required stamps and the existing bond was duly stamped.
High Courts had expressed conflicting views on whether such a bond was governed by the Court-fees Act or the Indian Stamp Act.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed, the orders rejecting the application were set aside, and the application to set aside the ex parte decree was granted. The ex parte decree was set aside and the suit was to proceed from the point at which it had been decreed ex parte.
issues.legal_principle: The proviso to Section 17(1) of the Provincial Small Cause Courts Act, 1887 requires an applicant seeking to set aside an ex parte decree to deposit the amount due or provide security as previously directed by the court. Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides for setting aside an ex parte decree. The court noted the conflicting approaches in Kalapati Peda Pitchamma v. Chiruvelia, AIR 1935 Mad 380, and Babu Rao Keshav Rao v. Kalavatibai Amrut Rao, AIR 1940 Bom 275, followed in Kasemali v. Ajovendra Paul, AIR 1956 Cal 375. It expressly left unresolved whether Article 6 of Schedule II to the Court-fees Act or Article 57 of the Indian Stamp Act governed the bond. In the circumstances, a litigant should not be shut out on a procedural technicality after acting on an uncertain state of law and curing the defect as the court directed.

rule.if: appeal_from_refusal_to_set_aside_ex_parte_decree and timely_security_request and bond_furnished_within_time and stamp_defect_cured_on_court_direction and conflicting_legal_views

predicates.appeal_from_refusal_to_set_aside_ex_part: The proceeding is an appeal from a refusal to set aside an ex parte decree in a small-causes case.
predicates.timely_security_request: The judgment-debtor applied within the applicable period for permission to provide security instead of depositing the full amount due.
predicates.bond_furnished_within_time: The judgment-debtor furnished the security bond within the applicable period.
predicates.stamp_defect_cured_on_court_direction: After the court identified a stamping defect, the judgment-debtor supplied the required stamps as directed.
predicates.conflicting_legal_views: Different High Courts had reached conflicting views on the stamp requirements for the bond.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns refusal to set aside an ex parte decree, and the judgment-debtor timely requested security, furnished the bond in time, cured its stamping defect as directed, and faced conflicting legal views, the application to set aside the decree is granted.
